Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 110, verse 1:

Tafsir of Surat "al-Nasr" (The Help), which is Madani by consensus. It is also called Surat al-Tawdi' (the Farewell Surah). It has three verses. It is the last surah to have been revealed in its entirety, as stated by Ibn Abbas in Sahih Muslim. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the help of Allah comes, and the conquest,﴾ (1)

Al-nasr (help) means aid, derived from their saying: "The rain has helped (nasara) the land," when it aids its vegetation after its drought. The poet said: [[It is the shepherd addressing horses.

(From Lisan al-Arab, root n-s-r.)]] "When the sacred month has passed, then depart, and help (insuri) the land of Amir, leaving the territory of Tamim."

It is also related as:

"When the sacred month has entered, then pass beyond the territory of Tamim, and help the land of Amir."

It is said: "He helped him (nasarahu) against his enemy, yanşuruhu, nasran," meaning he aided him. The noun is nusrah. "Istansarahu 'ala 'aduwwihi" means he asked him to help him against his enemy. "Tanasaru" means some of them helped one another. Then it has been said: the intended meaning of this help is the Messenger's victory over the Quraysh, related from al-Tabari. It has also been said: he helped him against those among the disbelievers who fought him, for the final outcome of the victory was in his favour. As for al-Fath (the conquest), it is the conquest of Makkah, related from al-Hasan, Mujahid and others. Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the conquest of the cities and palaces. It has also been said: the conquest of all the lands. It has also been said: what He opened for him of knowledge. "Idha" here carries the meaning of "qad" (indeed), i.e., "the help of Allah has indeed come," because its revelation was after the conquest. It is also possible that its meaning is: "when it comes to you."

**Allah's words:** ﴿And you see the people﴾, meaning the Arabs and others, ﴿entering the religion of Allah in multitudes﴾, meaning in groups, ﴿one group after another﴾. This happened when Makkah was conquered. The Arabs said: "Since Muhammad has prevailed over the people of the Sacred Precinct, and Allah had protected them from the Companions of the Elephant, you have no power (yadan) against him." [[i.e., strength, capacity.]] So they embraced Islam in multitudes, nation after nation.

Al-Dahhak said: "The ummah (community, here a group) is forty men." 

Ikrimah and Muqatil said: "By 'the people' he meant the people of Yemen. Seven hundred men came from Yemen as believers, obedient, some of them calling the adhan, some reciting the Qur'an, and some saying tahlil. The Prophet ﷺ was delighted by this, and Umar and Ibn Abbas wept."

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet ﷺ recited: "When the help of Allah and the victory come, and the people of Yemen come, with tender hearts, gentle dispositions, generous hearts, and great fear of Allah, they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes."

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Yemen have come to you. They are gentler of heart and softer of soul. Understanding (al-fiqh) is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni."

It is also narrated that he ﷺ said: "Indeed, I find the breath (nafas) of your Lord coming from the direction of Yemen." [[Ibn al-Athir said: (It is borrowed from the breath of air that one inhales into the body, which cools its heat and balances it. Or from the breath of the wind that one smells, and finds relief in it. Or from the fragrance of a garden, whose pleasant scent brings relief. One says: "You are in ease (nafas) regarding your affair," and "You are in ease regarding your life," meaning in space and freedom before sickness, old age, and the like.)]] 

Here there are two interpretations (ta'wil, i.e., explanation of meaning): The first is that it means relief, because their Islam followed in multitudes. The second is that the meaning is that Allah relieved the distress of His Prophet ﷺ through the people of Yemen, who are the Ansar (the Helpers).

Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Indeed, people have entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and they will leave it in multitudes.'" This was mentioned by al-Mawardi. The wording of al-Tha'labi is: Abu Ammar said: Jabir told me, [saying] to Jabir: Jabir asked me about the condition of the people, so I informed him about their disagreement and division, and he began to weep and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'Indeed, people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and they will leave the religion of Allah in multitudes.'"

The Quranic quotations are marked with ﴿ ﴾ throughout.

Allah's words, ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾: that is, when you pray, increase in this. It was also said: the meaning of "glorify" (sabbih) is "pray" (salli). From Ibn Abbas: "with the praise of your Lord" means praising Him for what He has given you of victory and conquest. "Seek His forgiveness" means ask Allah for forgiveness. It was also said: the intended meaning of "glorify" (fasabbih) is tanzih (declaring Allah free of what is not befitting to Him), that is, declare Him free of what is not permissible for Him, together with thanking Him. "Seek His forgiveness" means ask Allah for forgiveness while persistently remembering Him. The first interpretation is the most apparent.

The imams narrated (and the wording is that of al-Bukhari) from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "After ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾ was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he did not pray a prayer without saying: [Glory be to You, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me]." She also said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to frequently say in his bowing and prostration: [Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me]. He was interpreting the Qur'an."

In the non-Sahih (collections): Umm Salama said: "In the last part of his life, the Prophet (ﷺ) did not stand, sit, come or go without saying: [Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I ask Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance]." He said: "Indeed I was commanded to say it," and then he recited ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾ to its end.

Abu Hurayra said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) strove exceedingly after its revelation, until his feet swelled, his body became emaciated, his smiling decreased and his weeping increased."

Ikrimah said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) never exerted himself more in matters of the Hereafter than he did at the time of its revelation."

Muqatil said: "When it was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to his companions, among them Abu Bakr, Umar and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. They rejoiced and felt glad tidings, but al-Abbas wept. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: [What makes you weep, O uncle?] He said: 'Your soul has been announced to you.' He said: [It is as you say]. He then lived after it sixty [[Variant in al-Tabari and al-Kashshaf: (two years).]] days, and was not seen laughing or joyful during them."

It was also said: it was revealed at Mina after the Days of Tashriq, during the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada'). Umar and al-Abbas wept, and it was said to them: "This is a day of joy." They said: "Rather, in it is the announcement of the Prophet's (ﷺ) death." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: [You both have spoken truly; my soul has been announced to me].

In al-Bukhari and others, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab used to admit the people of Badr (Ahl Badr), and he admitted me with them. Some of them felt resentment at this and said: 'He admits this youth with us, when we have sons like him!' Umar said to them: 'He is someone you know well [[That is, because of his intelligence and great knowledge, or because of his kinship with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).]].' One day he admitted them, and admitted me with them. He asked them about this surah, ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾. They said: 'Allah the Mighty and Majestic commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) that when victory was granted to him, he should seek His forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.' Umar asked: 'What do you say, O Ibn Abbas?' I said: 'It is not so. Rather, Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of the approach of his appointed time (ajal). He said: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾, and that is the sign of your death. ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾.' Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Do you blame me for it?'" In al-Bukhari, Umar said: "I know nothing about it except what you say."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it, saying: "Umar used to question me in the presence of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to him: 'Do you ask him when we have sons like him?' Umar said to him: 'He is from the place of knowledge that we know.' He asked him about this verse, ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾. I said: 'It is only the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which Allah informed him of,' and I recited the surah to its end. Umar said to him: 'By Allah, I know nothing about it except what you know.'" He said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

If it is asked: "What is there for the Prophet (ﷺ) to be forgiven, that he should be commanded to seek forgiveness?" It is answered: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in his supplication: [My Lord, forgive me my sin and my ignorance, and my excess in all my affairs, and what You know better than I do. O Allah, forgive me my mistakes and my deliberate acts, my ignorance and my jesting, and all of that is with me. O Allah, forgive me what I have sent forward and what I have put off, what I have made public and what I have kept private. You are the One who brings forward and You are the One who puts off, and You are over all things Powerful]. He (ﷺ) used to consider his self to be small in the face of the greatness of the blessing Allah had bestowed on him, and he regarded his shortcoming in fulfilling the due of that as a sin.

It may also mean: be attached to Him, asking and desiring, humbling yourself, seeing your shortcoming in fulfilling the rights (of Allah), so that you do not stop at looking at your deeds. It was also said: seeking forgiveness is an act of worship which is obligatory upon us, not for the sake of obtaining forgiveness, but as worship. It was said: this is an admonition to his community, lest they feel secure and abandon seeking forgiveness. It was also said: ﴿and seek His forgiveness﴾ means: seek forgiveness for your community.

(﴿Indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾): that is, He accepts the repentance of those who glorify Him and those who seek forgiveness; He turns to them, shows them mercy and accepts their repentance. If he (peace be upon him), who is protected from sin (ma'sum), is commanded to seek forgiveness, what then is the assumption regarding others?

Muslim narrated from Aisha, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to frequently say: [Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I ask Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance]." She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I see you frequently saying: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I ask Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance."' He said: 'My Lord informed me that I would see a sign in my community, and when I see it I should frequently say: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I ask Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. I have seen it: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come﴾ — the conquest of Makkah — and you have seen people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes. So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance.'"

(Ibn Umar said: "This surah was revealed at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and then ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you﴾ [[Verse 3 of Surat al-Ma'idah.]] [al-Ma'idah: 3] was revealed. After these two, the Prophet (ﷺ) lived eighty days. Then the verse of kalalah [[End of Surat al-Nisa'.]] was revealed, and he lived after it fifty days. Then ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ [[Verse 128 of Surat al-Tawbah.]] [al-Tawbah: 128] was revealed, and he lived after it thirty-five days. Then ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾ [[Verse 281 of Surat al-Baqarah.]] was revealed, and he lived after it twenty-one days." Muqatil said: "seven days." It was also said other than this, as has been explained earlier in "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 3, p. 375.]]. And praise be to Allah.)
